---
description: How the map tools are called - the six for a place's map of squares (map_lay, map_edit, map_place, map_view, map_measure, map_door), and the four for the world's maps of places, found by search (world_map_place, world_map_link, world_map_settings, world_keep). It says how to call them, not when. Delete this file and an agent that holds or finds one of them is given no such guide.
---
A square is `[column, row]`, counted from 1 at the top left, with north up. Name a place, a person or a thing as the world does, or by its id.

map_lay lays a map for a place: `rows`, top first, one symbol to a square (`#` wall, `.` floor, `+` door, a space nothing, and the symbols of the `legend` you give), or, with no rows, a walled room of `width` by `height` with `doors` as squares of its wall; `feet` is how wide a square is. A symbol no legend names reads as floor and is reported, and the map stands as assumed. Where the place has a map already, the one you lay goes over it in this chat only: the answer says so, the world's own map is untouched, and a swipe takes it back. A map takes at most 64 rows of 64 squares; a larger one is answered with the most it takes: lay it in parts, each room its own place over its square of a coarser map, or with wider squares. `over` and `square` lay it over one square of a coarser map, for the place that square holds, or for a new place named by `place` where it holds none; the square then opens onto the new map, and whoever stood on it stands on no square of the new map until placed. `remove` true takes a map laid in play out of this chat's world again.

map_edit changes part of a map without redrawing it, a drawn map or a grid the world wrote without one alike: `strokes`, each a `symbol` put on `squares`, in a `rect` between two corners or along a `line`, and a `legend` to add or change symbols (null takes one out; `"blocks": true` for a square nobody walks through). What a stroke reaches off the map is left out and counted in the answer. A symbol no legend names is read as floor and reported, so name it in the legend; the squares drawn with it are recorded as assumed. `things` makes a thing of a fixture drawn on the map, by one `square` it is drawn on, with a `name` where it is not the terrain's: its squares become floor, and the thing stands there with their footprint, blocking what the terrain blocked.

map_place takes `pieces`, one object for each person or thing: `who` and one of `square`, `near` (beside someone), `zone`, `on` (lying on a thing, sharing its square) or `lift` (off the map); `walk` true has it walk there, and the answer gives the way and the time it took; `size` and `blocks` (way, view, both or none) give a footprint. A piece may take its own `source`, `precision` and `standing`, over the call's: one call can record a position from the prose as established and another, by plain sense, as assumed. Each position is recorded as you give it, and only a square that does not exist is refused: one off the map, or at a place with no map, where the answer names map_lay, what is kept there by zone or words, and the near places that have a map. A `near` with no free square, or a full `zone`, puts the piece on the nearest square all the same, reports who it stands over, and records that square as assumed. A zone the map lacks, or someone who stands on no square, stays as words where they are, with a report. Someone at another place is brought here first, and that is reported.

map_door takes the door's `door` square and its `state`: open, closed or locked. map_view shows the map as text, around a `centre` (a square, or someone) when it is too large to show whole; at a place with no map it answers that, with what is kept there by zone or words and the near places that have a map. map_measure reads and changes nothing: from a spot, `to` gives the distance, whether the two see each other, the cover one has from the other and the way between, its time at `speed` squares a round where you give one; `within` gives who is in range; `area` (burst, cone, line or cube) with its `size`, and `toward` for a cone, a line or a cube, gives the squares it covers, as runs by row, laid by the world's ruleset's grid rule or else the settings'. Someone who stands on no square is told as such, with where they are kept, and the rest of the call is measured.

The four found by search change this chat's own copy of its world's maps of places: it plays at once, goes with the turn, and stays the chat's until kept. world_map_place puts a place on a `map` (by id or title) with its `name` and its `x` and `y` on that map, counted from 0 (on a grid map, its column and row); naming a place on it in `place`, it moves or renames it, gives the map that draws its inside (`opens`, a map you lay first with map_lay), or takes it off with `remove`. world_map_link links `from` and `to` on a `map` by `mode` (walk, road, offroad or water) and `minutes`, both ways unless `one_way`; `remove` takes a link out. world_map_settings takes only what changes of `display`, `grid_movement`, `sight_radius` and `travel_simulation`. world_keep copies into the world's draft what you name of what this chat changed (`maps`, `places`, `paths`, and `settings` true); named nothing, it lists what the chat has changed.

Each write but world_keep also takes `source`, and `precision` and `standing` where you know them.

    map_lay {"place": "The Cellar", "rows": ["#####+##", "#......#", "#......#", "########"], "source": {"from": "prose", "message": "m-12"}}
    map_place {"at": "The Common Room", "pieces": [{"who": "Wren", "square": [6, 5]}, {"who": "Bram", "near": "Wren"}, {"who": "lantern", "on": "long table"}], "source": {"from": "prose", "message": "m-12"}}
    map_measure {"from": "Wren", "to": "Bram"}
    tool_use {"name": "world_map_link", "args": {"map": "Thornbury", "from": "The Bluebird", "to": "Market Square", "mode": "walk", "minutes": 5, "source": {"from": "prose", "message": "m-12"}}}
